summary: Error message in PairTersoffMODKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/mod/kk), a copy-paste leftover from pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- identical string to src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs `pair_style tersoff/mod/kk` with `-pk kokkos neigh full`; the error names a style they are not using, sending them to the wrong input line.
suggested_fix: Change the string to name tersoff/mod/kk (and check the same copy in pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp / pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp).

summary: Device kernel calls the host math function pow() unqualified instead of Kokkos::pow(), violating KOKKOS rule 4 (all other math in the same block uses Kokkos::).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:406-407 `const KK_FLOAT a_ij = (static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.8854)*global_a_0) /\n        static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_i,0.23) + pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_j,0.23));` inside KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION tersoff_zbl_compute; contrast line 405 `Kokkos::pow(global_e,...)` and lines 411-416 which all use Kokkos::exp. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos:: math in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Compiling tersoff/zbl/kk for a backend whose device math library does not provide an unqualified ::pow overload (SYCL/HIP variants) fails to compile or silently falls back to the host implementation.
suggested_fix: Replace both calls with Kokkos::pow(...); better still, precompute a_ij and premult once per param in setup_params instead of per pair.

summary: Error message in PairTersoffZBLKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/zbl/kk).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:133-134 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- copy-paste from src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs pair_style tersoff/zbl/kk with `-pk kokkos neigh full` and gets an error naming a style not in the input.
suggested_fix: Name the actual style in the message.

summary: Local `eng` is left uninitialized when eflag==0 but is still passed to ev_tally() when only vflag_either is set.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:422-440: `KK_FLOAT frep, eng;` ... `if (eflag)\n      eng = (1.0 - fermi_k(...)) * eng_z + fermi_k(...) * eng_t;` ... `if (vflag_either || eflag_atom) this->template ev_tally<NEIGHFLAG>(ev,i,j,eng,frep,delx,dely,delz);`. The equivalent code in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:386 computes `eng` unconditionally.
failure_scenario: `compute pressure` without any energy output: EVFLAG=1, eflag=0, vflag_global=1 -> ev_tally is called with an indeterminate `eng`. ev_tally only reads epair under `if (eflag_atom)` (which implies eflag), so no wrong numbers today, but the read of an indeterminate value is fragile and warns under -Wmaybe-uninitialized.
suggested_fix: Initialize `KK_FLOAT eng = 0.0;` (or compute it unconditionally as tersoff/mod does).

summary: The KOKKOS M-site pre-kernel drops the CPU styles' check that the two atoms found by tag+1/tag+2 really are of type typeH, so a mis-ordered water topology silently produces wrong M sites instead of an error.
failure_scenario: A data file where an O atom's tag+1 / tag+2 are not its two H atoms (e.g. water mixed with other molecules, or ions numbered between the water atoms): tip4p/cut and tip4p/long abort with a clear error, tip4p/cut/kk and tip4p/long/kk build M sites from the wrong atoms and silently return wrong forces and energies.
suggested_fix: In the TagPairTIP4PNewsite kernel, also set d_hneigh(i,0) = -1 (or a separate error flag) when type(iH1) != m_typeH || type(iH2) != m_typeH, and report the distinct 'incorrect atom type' error from finalize().

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() gates on `r < d_cutsq(itype,jtype)`, comparing a distance against a SQUARED cutoff, and runs the knot search before the gate, so calls with r past the cutoff walk off the end of d_n2b_knot and evaluate the spline with a bogus index.
failure_scenario: `pair_style uf3 2` (single_enable stays 1, see src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:122-125) plus `pair_write 1 1 500 r 0.5 8.0 out.txt`: for every r >= cut the while-loop indexes d_n2b_knot past its last knot (extent max_num_knots_2b), reading out of bounds and/or looping until it happens to find a larger value, then constants_2b(...) is read at that bogus start_index; uf3/kk returns garbage (or crashes) where plain uf3 returns 0.
suggested_fix: Move the knot search inside the guard and compare rsq against d_cutsq (or r against cut[itype][jtype]), exactly as PairUF3::single does.

summary: PairUF3Kokkos::single() does not scale the returned force by factor_lj, so special-bond scaled pairs get an unscaled force while the energy is scaled.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1648 `fforce = static_cast<double>(dnconstants_2b(interaction_id, start_index - 1, 0));` ... line 1659 `return factor_lj * value;` -- the CPU base src/ML-UF3/pair_uf3.cpp:1857 does `fforce = factor_lj * force_2b;` before `return factor_lj * value;` (line 1878).
failure_scenario: Any caller of single() with factor_lj != 1 (special_bonds scaling, e.g. `compute group/group` style callers or a tabulation over bonded pairs) gets fforce too large by 1/factor_lj from uf3/kk while plain uf3 returns the scaled value.
suggested_fix: Multiply the accumulated fforce by factor_lj, matching PairUF3::single.

summary: All UF3 spline coefficient/knot views are hardcoded to LMPDeviceType instead of the class's DeviceType template parameter, yet they are read from KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION kernels that are instantiated for LMPHostType as well (uf3/kk/host).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.h:88-108 declares e.g. `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> d_coefficients_2b;`, `Kokkos::View<int **, LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> map2b;`, `Kokkos::View<KK_FLOAT **[16], LMPDeviceLayout, LMPDeviceType> constants_2b;` (and 10 more). These are read in the device kernels: src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:560 `int interaction_id = map2b(itype, jtype);` and 562/573 inside `twobody()`, and 619/636/647 inside `threebody()`, which run under `Kokkos::RangePolicy<DeviceType,...>` (lines 796/800). src/KOKKOS/pair_uf3_kokkos.cpp:1664-1666 explicitly instantiates `PairUF3Kokkos<LMPHostType>` under LMP_KOKKOS_GPU. This is the same defect class the KOKKOS rules describe for `DAT::` per-atom views (.github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 3).
failure_scenario: On a CUDA/HIP build, `pair_style uf3/kk/host` (or `-k on ... -sf kk` with the host back end selected) runs the kernels on the host while these views live in device memory: Kokkos' memory-space access check aborts at the first `map2b(itype,jtype)`. On a CPU-only build both spaces coincide, so the defect is invisible.
suggested_fix: Change the memory space of these views (and d_cut_3b_list) from LMPDeviceType to the class template parameter DeviceType, as the neighbor-short views at lines 179-180 already do.

summary: `kokkosable = 1;` is commented out in the PairUF3Kokkos constructor, so VerletKokkos treats uf3/kk as a non-KOKKOS pair style and turns on auto_sync for the whole pair compute.
failure_scenario: Every uf3/kk step forces a full host/device round trip of x/f/energy/virial through auto_sync, negating the point of the port; also src/force.cpp:208's kokkosable sanity check is bypassed.
suggested_fix: Uncomment `kokkosable = 1;` (and verify the style really keeps its data device-resident) or document why it must stay off.
